To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a linear, nonuniform 77 GHz MIMO FMCV radar array can be designed and built.
The design of a non-uniform antenna is more complicated than the design of a uniform antenna.
a particle swarm optimization based design of an array for a 3D radar system is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, high-performance, low-cost radar systems.
the design and implementation of a 77 GHz MIMO FMCV radar.
the design of a 2D non-uniform antenna element for an automotive radar system at 77 GHz.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the particle swarm optimization is a very powerful tool for designing antenna arrays.
the non-uniform spacing of the antenna array in combination with a MIMO system is a promising approach to achieve a high angular resolution in a 77-GHZ automotive radar system.
the particle swarm optimization offers the best results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the particle swarm optimized array has the best performance, followed by the stepwise brute force array and the brute force array.
the non-uniform antenna spacing in combination with MIMO offers superior performance compared to uniform spacing with the same number of elements.

a linear non-unform array with 5 elements and a spacing of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 mm offers a superior performance in terms of side lobe level, main beam width, and cross polarization level compared to a classical half-wavelength uniform linear array with 5 equally spaced antenna elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MIMO principle in combination with the non-uniform antenna spacing offers a superior performance over a uniform array with an equal amount of elements.
the non-uniform antenna arrays can offer better performance than uniform arrays, but at the cost of a much higher complexity.
the particle swarm optimization can be used to design an antenna array with an arbitrary element spacing.
